thread:
alex: heads-up — we saw a production fallback in eu-west where requests from Dedicated tier (p50 latency target) got routed to a variant that uses a different tokenizer. tool-calling failed downstream. not sure we should silently fall back in this case :thinking_face:
marie: ugh, which part failed? tokenizer mismatch or context-length chop?
zhu: tokenizer parity. variant has a byte-pair tokenizer vs canonical one — embeddings/tool-calls expect same token ids for function args. we rejected in postprocess with `ToolCallError(TokenMismatch)`
samir: can you paste the route + variant metadata? want to understand router decision criteria (latency vs compatibility).
az: (ops-bot) route: customer-tier=dedicated -> prefer: variant-a (fast-q4), fallback chain: variant-b (compat), variant-c (cheap).
zhu: variant-a was out of capacity so router picked variant-b, but our compatibility labels are incomplete — variant-b was marked 'tools: yes' but tokenizer field was empty so router assumed compatible.
marie: so labels are incomplete. do we need a stronger compatibility matrix check at router-time rather than relying on metadata? i think console should show "fallback -> variant-b (tokenizer-parity-unknown)" with warning icon
samir: agree. options: 1) conservative router: require explicit tokenizer parity flag. 2) runtime preflight: do a tiny dry-run tokenization/signature check before routing (adds ~5-10ms). 3) explicit reject with 409 and surface to caller. tradeoffs on latency and UX.
nina: from SRE POV, silent mismatches cause weird error patterns in downstream services. prefer explicit rejection or telemetry + alerting so customers can opt-in for permissive fallback.
zhu: implementable plan: runtime exposes `compat_check(kind=tokenizer|context|toolcall)` endpoint that returns pass/warn/fail. router calls it when a variant is candidate. we cache results per model+variant for 24h.
marie: console UX: show the compat_check matrix per model version, and for rollouts show which variant passed/failed checks. add a reason badge on the rollout timeline.
samir: also need metric: `routing.fallback_reason` with tags {tier,region,from_variant,to_variant,reason}. Dashboards should have a small alert if fallback_reason=tokenizer_mismatch > 10/min for a customer.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/compat-check-api -> staging (zhu)
zhu: i'll PR the compat endpoint today. will default to warn if unknown, but router config flag `require_strict_compat=true` for enterprise customers.
marie: owners: samir -> router change + dashboards, zhu -> runtime endpoint + cache, me -> console badges + docs. timeline: staging EOD, canary tomorrow.
alex: thanks. quick follow-ups: (1) add a test in router e2e that simulates tokenizer mismatch, (2) add an integration test for tool-call path to catch TokenMismatch.
samir: added to my board. will also add a small UI toggle in Console -> Rollouts to "allow heuristic fallback" for lower tiers.
nina: fyi i'm adding a SLO runbook note: if tokenizer_mismatch alert fires, escalate to runtime+model-onboarding.
marie: perfect. I'll update the rollout checklist & customer-facing docs to call out tokenizer parity requirement for tool-calling. :white_check_mark:
alex: ok closing — thanks team, let's sync in tomorrow standup if any blockers.
